content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of ionic compounds
Explain the properties of ionic compounds in terms of structure
Explain why ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved
Ionic compounds have a characteristic structure that gives them distinctive properties. Understanding the
structure helps explain why ionic compounds behave the way they do.
- regular three-dimensional structures containing billions of ions.
Ions are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern
Each positive ion is surrounded by negative ions
Each negative ion is surrounded by positive ions
Strong electrostatic forces act in all directions
Each Na⁺ ion is surrounded by 6 Cl⁻ ions
Each Cl⁻ ion is surrounded by 6 Na⁺ ions
This maximises the attractive forces between oppositely charged ions
The formula NaCl represents the ratio of ions, not individual molecules
Ionic compounds do NOT exist as molecules. They exist as giant structures with no distinct molecules.
Strong electrostatic forces between ions require a lot of energy to break
Regular structure is rigid but can crack if layers shift
Water molecules can surround and separate ions
Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points because:
is needed to overcome these forces
Energy is needed to separate the ions
Why MgO Has a Higher Melting Point Than NaCl
Magnesium oxide (Mg²⁺ O²⁻) has a higher melting point than sodium chloride (Na⁺ Cl⁻) because:
More energy needed to overcome the stronger forces
Solid ionic compounds do NOT conduct electricity because:
Ions cannot move to carry charge
Molten ionic compounds DO conduct because:
Ions can carry charge through the liquid
Dissolved ionic compounds DO conduct because:
Ions can carry charge through the solution
Strong forces hold ions firmly in place
Like charges end up next to each other
Repulsion causes the crystal to shatter
Many ionic compounds dissolve in water because:
This overcomes the attraction between the ions
Not all ionic compounds dissolve in water. Some have very strong ionic bonds that water cannot overcome.
Use key phrases: "strong electrostatic forces," "ions free to move," "ions fixed in position"
When explaining conductivity, specify whether ions are mobile or fixed
Saying ionic compounds are made of molecules
Ionic compounds form giant ionic lattices, not molecules
Saying ionic bonds break when an ionic compound melts
The electrostatic forces between ions are overcome, but the ions still exist
Forgetting that dissolved ionic compounds conduct electricity
Both molten AND dissolved ionic compounds conduct

The force of attraction between opposite charges
Breaks or shatters when force is applied
In liquid state due to heating above melting point
Ionic compounds form giant ionic lattice structures

due to strong electrostatic forces between ions
ions are free to move and carry charge
layers can shift, causing like charges to repel
